transcript:
>> This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
>> Live from NPR News, I'm Giles Snyder.
A source tells NPR the reason the U.S. military withdrew its bombers from a base in the U.K.
was a threat of an Iranian drone attack.
NPR's Quill Lawrence reports on the removal of all 12 B-1 bombers.
>> A U.S. government official not authorized to speak publicly confirmed to NPR that fears
of a drone attack on behalf of Iran caused the U.S. to withdraw all the American bombers
from Fairford Air Base in England.
The base has been used for bombing sorties in the U.S. and Israeli war with Iran.
Late last month, British authorities arrested five men traveling in white vans near the
air base in the pre-dawn hours.
The men were later released after no explosives were found.
British officials say the men remain under investigation and two more arrests have been
made in the past week, including a British-Iranian dual national.
Quill Lawrence, NPR News.
>> With roughly four weeks to go until midterm election day, more than a million voters have
already cast their ballots and money is pouring into political ads across key House and Senate
contests.
NPR's Stephen Fowler on what Democrats are signaling with their money moves.
>> Just this week, the Democratic House campaign arm added six districts to its red to blue
target list of flips that's now up to 46 seats.
A lot of it's aspirational and stretches into places that Trump won by double digits, like
a House district in Little Rock, Arkansas, for example.
At the same time, though, Republicans have invested considerable money in some of these
places too to boost their candidates and attack Democrats, as polls show this combination
potentially of a supercharged Democratic turnout, independents backing the Democrats and a meaningful
amount of Republicans staying home.
>> President Trump was asked Tuesday about that taxpayer-funded ad campaign headed into
the November midterms, a day after saying he would now pay for the ads using money from
his super PAC.
He did not commit to reimbursing the millions already spent, telling reporters in his words
will decide whether to repay the funds.
Cornell University has named a former Justice Department leader to head an investigation
into how the school handles reports of sexual assault.
Here's NPR's Jacqueline Diaz reporting.
>> Former acting US Attorney General Sally Yates will lead the internal review into how
Cornell responded when the now former student reported being drugged and repeatedly raped
at a fraternity on campus.
Yates was picked by a newly formed special committee of the Cornell University Board
of Trustees.
She will also examine the school's policies on how it prevents in response to sexual harassment,
assault, and other misconduct on campus.
This all comes after a former student filed a lawsuit against the school last month.
The student, who goes by Jane Doe, alleges failings in how Cornell administrators handled
her case.
Yates's probe is separate from a reopening of the criminal case, which is being led by
New York AG Letitia James.
Jacqueline Diaz, NPR News.
>> And you're listening to NPR News.
Lawyers for convicted killer Krista Pike say they will be in court later today.
They're asking a judge for a court order to preserve evidence from Pike's failed execution,
claiming the state of Tennessee violated Pike's rights by subjecting her to cruel and unusual
punishment.
In a statement, Pike's lawyers say she has regained consciousness and is speaking after
surviving two doses of a lethal injection drug.
Obesity rates in children and adolescents have quadrupled to more than 170 million people
since 1990.
And Bear's Gabrielle Emmanuelle reports on the World Health Organization's release of
its first guidelines on how to treat that age group.
>> For children under the age of 10 who are obese, the WHO is emphasizing dietary changes
and physical activity.
They are not recommending surgery or weight loss medications like GLP1 for children.
Luz Maria de Regil is with the WHO.
>> There is not enough evidence that trials are starting.
The medications that have been tested are not proven.
>> She says they are also considering the long-term effect in cost of medications as well as the
long-term cost of obesity, which is estimated to be trillions of dollars each year worldwide.
Gabrielle Emmanuelle, NPR News.
>> Lionel Messi has played his last international soccer match after helping Argentina win a
World Cup and two South American championships during his more than 20 years playing for
his country's national team.
Messi is stepping away from international soccer.
Messi will continue playing for major league soccer's Inter Miami.
I'm Jael Snyder and this is NPR News.

More than one million voters cast ballots as Democrats and Republicans pour money into midterm election ads
Democratic House campaign arm adds six districts to its target list, now up to 46 potential seat flips
President Trump says his words will decide whether to repay millions in taxpayer-funded midterm campaign ads
Cornell University names former Acting US Attorney General Sally Yates to investigate sexual assault handling
Lawyers for convicted killer Krista Pike seek court order to preserve evidence from her failed execution in Tennessee
World Health Organization releases first guidelines on treating obesity in children and adolescents
Lionel Messi retires from international soccer after over 20 years playing for Argentina
